system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran tit‑for‑tat escalation and regional spillover
system_description.narrative_summary: A cycle of kinetic strikes, maritime confrontations, and sanctions between the United States and Iran is dominating the reporting, producing reciprocal military, economic and diplomatic reactions that risk wider regionalization (Israel–Lebanon, Gulf states) and disruption of oil flows. Treated as an open system, the dynamic is driven by interacting flows: direct military actions, proxy strikes, sanctions and financial choke points, diplomatic maneuvers (IAEA/UN referrals) and domestic political signals; these generate reinforcing feedbacks (tit‑for‑tat retaliation, rallying of supporters) and balancing pressures (diplomatic restraint, force protection, economic costs). External inputs (U.S. and Israeli political cycles, global energy demand, international institutions) and outputs (regional instability, oil price/insurance shocks, force deployments) continually reshape the trajectory.
system_description.scope: State and state‑backed military exchanges (US, Iran), maritime incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf, sanctions/financial measures and their enablers, proxy actors (Hezbollah, Israel, Gulf states), diplomatic/institutional actions (IAEA/UN), effects on energy infrastructure and US force posture; domestic political signaling from key actors that conditions decision making.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and maritime insurance
International institutions and norms (IAEA, UN Security Council)
U.S. domestic politics and electoral cycles

variables.name: Kinetic strike rate
variables.description: Rate of direct kinetic military strikes between state-level actors in the theater.

variables.name: Proxy attack rate
variables.description: Frequency of attacks and operations undertaken by state‑backed non‑state proxy actors.

variables.name: Maritime incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of naval confrontations, interdictions, and hostile interactions at sea within the maritime chokepoints.

variables.name: Sanctions intensity
variables.description: Aggregate severity, scope, and targeted breadth of economic penalties and trade restrictions applied against an actor or sector.

variables.name: Financial chokepoint effectiveness
variables.description: Degree to which financial restrictions and interdictions impede cross‑border payments, banking links, and revenue flows.

variables.name: Force deployment level
variables.description: Scale and concentration of forward military forces, platforms, and assets deployed in the region.

variables.name: Oil flow disruption rate
variables.description: Rate at which crude and refined product shipments, terminals, or chokepoints experience interruptions or attacks.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Short‑term variability and market volatility in regional and global oil price benchmarks attributable to the theater.

variables.name: Maritime insurance premium
variables.description: Level of insurance premia and risk surcharges applied to shipping transiting the contested maritime zones.

variables.name: Diplomatic action intensity
variables.description: Pace and intensity of diplomatic maneuvers, institutional referrals, and multilateral political actions addressing the dispute.

variables.name: Domestic political signaling
variables.description: Strength and frequency of domestic political rhetoric, electoral signaling, and internal political pressures that condition decision making.

variables.name: Retaliation momentum
variables.description: Reinforcing tendency and velocity of reciprocal tit‑for‑tat actions that amplify cyclical escalation.

variables.name: Force protection constraints
variables.description: Level of operational constraints and restrictions arising from force‑protection risk tolerances and rules of engagement.

variables.name: Civilian disruption level
variables.description: Magnitude of civilian casualties, displacement, infrastructure damage, and humanitarian stress in affected areas.

variables.name: Attribution confidence
variables.description: Degree of certainty among actors and observers in attributing responsibility for hostile incidents.

variables.name: Regional escalation spread rate
variables.description: Speed and extent to which conflict dynamics and hostile actions diffuse to adjacent actors, territories, or frontlines.

catalysts.title: U.S. threat to strike Pickaxe Mountain
catalysts.description: Public U.S. threat to hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain may precede a targeted kinetic strike, raising near‑term strike risk and reciprocal responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Trump says US may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain soon" — overt strike threat likely raises strike and retaliation risk.

catalysts.title: IAEA board push to refer Iran to UN Security Council
catalysts.description: Diplomatic push at the IAEA to send Iran to the UNSC could trigger multilateral political measures and open pathways for tougher penalties.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "US and allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council" — referral increases diplomatic and sanction pathways.

catalysts.title: Continuation/escalation of U.S. bank sanctions linked to Iran
catalysts.description: Following sanctions on a Turkish bank, the U.S. may expand financial penalties against banks and intermediaries, tightening Iran's financial access.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "U.S. sanctions Turkish bank..." and "US sanctions Turkish bank, two subsidiaries" — indicates ongoing sanctions campaign.

catalysts.title: U.S. probe into wedding strike
catalysts.description: U.S. investigation into a strike that likely used a U.S. munition may alter attribution, accountability, and spur diplomatic or retaliatory moves.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "US probes Iran wedding strike" and "Deadly strike...likely a direct hit by a US munition" — probe will affect attribution and responses.

catalysts.title: Renewed strikes on oil tankers and maritime exchanges
catalysts.description: Recent U.S. strikes on Iranian crude carriers and reciprocal firing near Hormuz point to a likely short‑term spike in maritime confrontations and tanker attacks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "US strikes three Iranian oil tankers" and "U.S. and Iran Trade Strikes...for Control of Hormuz" — maritime tit‑for‑tat likely to continue.

catalysts.title: Escalation along south Lebanon front involving Hezbollah
catalysts.description: Recent strikes and warnings around south Lebanon make further exchanges between Israel and Hezbollah likely, risking regional spillover.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Iran warns US against Israeli attack on south Lebanon ridge" and "Israel says it strikes southern Lebanon after Hezbollah drone launch".

catalysts.title: Prolonged U.S. force deployments in the region
catalysts.description: Longer deployments strain U.S. forces and imply sustained high deployment levels with implications for operations and force‑protection rules.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Longer Middle East Deployments Strain U.S. Forces as Iran Conflict Drags On" — indicates ongoing high deployment levels.

catalysts.title: U.S. efforts to keep Gulf crude flowing
catalysts.description: U.S. measures to keep Gulf crude shipments moving are likely to continue, reducing Iran's blockade leverage but maintaining operational exposure.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Iran’s oil blockade leverage weakens as U.S. keeps Gulf crude flowing" — US protection reduces disruption but sustains deployments.

catalysts.title: U.S. domestic political pressure shaping policy toward Israel/Iran
catalysts.description: Heightened domestic political campaigning and legislative actions tied to Israel increase political signaling that may constrain or steer U.S. policy choices.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Pro‑Israel groups fight to help Republicans keep control of Congress" and "US House passes bill..." — domestic politics intensifying signals.
